description: Slack tokens come in three shapes: bot (`xoxb-...`), user (`xoxp-...`), and app-level (`xapp-...`). Bot tokens are the right default — they survive workspace member changes and carry workspace-scoped permissions. User tokens authenticate as a human and inherit their channel membership. App-level tokens are for Socket Mode connections.

variants.description: `xoxb-...` token issued under a bot identity. Authenticates web API calls (chat.postMessage, files.upload, etc) via `Authorization: Bearer`. Right default for service-to-Slack integrations — the bot's permissions follow the OAuth scopes you granted at install time.

steps: Pick the app (or Create New App)
OAuth & Permissions → Scopes → add the Bot Token Scopes you need (`chat:write`, `channels:read`, …)
Install to Workspace (or Reinstall after scope changes)
Copy the Bot User OAuth Token (starts with `xoxb-`)
retrieval.notes: Bot tokens are workspace-scoped; the same Slack app installed in a different workspace gets a different token. Reinstall after adding scopes — the existing token does NOT auto-grant new scopes.

variants.description: `xoxp-...` token authenticating as a user. Inherits the human's channel membership and DMs — sensitive. Use only when a bot scope can't cover the action (e.g. `users.profile.write`).

steps: OAuth & Permissions → Scopes → add the User Token Scopes
Copy the User OAuth Token (starts with `xoxp-`)
retrieval.notes: User tokens leak the human's full channel surface — treat as sensitive even for read-only scopes. Prefer the bot variant whenever possible.

variants.description: `xapp-...` token for Socket Mode (and a small set of admin endpoints). NOT a substitute for bot / user tokens — pairs with them.

steps: Basic Information → App-Level Tokens → Generate Token and Scopes
Pick the connection scopes (`connections:write` for Socket Mode)
retrieval.notes: App-level tokens authenticate the Socket Mode WebSocket connection itself; the per-event payload still carries a separate bot or user token for the action.
